source_lines: liam: wait. thai. cyrus. are we okay after the satay incident??
brooke: i'll still double check for you. no satay, no dipping sauce, nothing crushed on top of the noodles. same as always
liam: ok so someone at work ate pad see ew at her desk and the whole floor smelled like it. i need thai
maya: thai. yes. i would fight someone for pad thai right now
maya: tight. one pricey lunch and i'm eating toast until august
liam: cheap thai is the best thai anyway
brooke: count me in, just nothing greasy. i've got climbing after work and i'd like to actually make it up the wall

elimination.downtown_monsoon_alley: peanut dip and crushed peanuts on noodles and salads, so it's out on the allergy
elimination.downtown_teak_door: peanut-free, thai and $, but almost everything is fried and greasy, which breaks Brooke's request (-1 star)
elimination.downtown_river_bell: peanut-free, thai and light, but the review says it costs more and the card shows $$, one tier over budget (-1 star)
elimination.downtown_koi_counter: peanut-free, $ and light, but it's sushi, not thai (misses the craving, -1 star)
elimination.downtown_orchid_row: peanut-free (confirmed by kitchen), thai, $, fresh and light. Meets everything

notes: The chat never says the word 'peanut'. Cyrus's allergy comes from the 'satay incident' line and Brooke's list (no satay, no dipping sauce, nothing crushed on the noodles). A returning player will pick it up easily. A player who starts at this level would have to work out that satay means peanuts, which is a fair inference but relies on what earlier levels set up.
Each decoy fails exactly one constraint and each failure is easy to read. The 'step up' wording in River Bell's review and its $$ card agree, so the price clue is consistent.
Maya's budget line ('one pricey lunch and i'm eating toast') is soft, but Liam's 'cheap thai' line backs it up. Nothing contradictory or unfair found.
